item.text: I’m auditing the four statements and all 20 arrows as written, then I’ll check the published BNS theorem itself because the draft explicitly leaves exact-statement debt. I’ll treat missing binders and carrier adaptation as semantic defects, not charitable shorthand.

item.text:
The blueprint is not execution-ready. Three faces reproduce the free-carrier/adaptedness defect, and at least eleven derivation arrows require materially stronger statements than their cited faces.

### Face audit

1. **BLOCKER — K-DICT is not well-posed and repeats the documented failure mode.**  
   “A correspondence Θ between corpus chain histories … and GMN types” does not bind either side to the same polynomial, canonical run, realized branch, or equivalence class of representatives. Structurally lawful `VTree` histories remain free carrier data. A global “correspondence” is also ambiguous between function, bijection, and relation. At the intended instance, this is not plausibly true as written.

2. **BLOCKER — K-READ also leaves carrier data free.**  
   “For every lawful history site `(H, ν)`” supplies structural lawfulness but no hypothesis that `H` is realized by, adapted to, or even compatible with `canDec x`. Per-site quantification avoids M03’s false per-tree uniformity, but it does not solve the separate free-history problem. The required comparison variables and level-transition maps are also unstated, so “depends only on” is not yet a proposition with a determinate Lean shape.

3. **BLOCKER — K-READ-δ silently exceeds BNS 3.13.**  
   BNS proves stability of OM factorizations under polynomial congruence; it does not prove locality of every corpus `ReadsOf` site, invariance of execution traces, or a bound on every read performed by a particular classifier. Thus the alleged “precision face” may be true only after substantial dictionary/run results, not directly from the citation.

4. **BLOCKER — K-RUN’s first two clauses are well-indexed, but its nonempty-locus clause reintroduces free formal chains.**  
   No-phantom and no-missing compare runs of `canDec x` with `T_can(canDec x)`, so they contain an adaptation index and are plausibly true. But “every formal fresh-assignment chain from a zc history has a witnessing polynomial” quantifies over formal chains without requiring that the chain be a semantic prefix or otherwise adapted. That is precisely the project’s documented failure pattern.

5. **BLOCKER — K-HALT lacks an adaptation condition on “every lift g.”**  
   A leaf is said to belong to “a realized run,” but the subsequent verdict is asserted for “every lift `g`” without saying that the same run is realized for `g`, that `g` lies in its read cylinder, or that it agrees through the necessary precision. NsFree does not supply this relationship. Read literally, the assertion is implausibly strong. The assembly clause is plausible only for a complete, polynomial-adapted tree.

### Derivation-map audit

6. **BLOCKER — Row 2 uses a stronger fiber statement than K-RUN no-phantom.**  
   > “no-phantom on the fiber: every realized run on a lift of `x ∈ Φ_t(V)` is a chain of `V` or a rostered extension”

   K-RUN only says a realized run is a prefix of its own polynomial’s semantic branch. It does not identify that branch with the fixed carrier `V`, nor prove invariance across the fiber.

7. **BLOCKER — Row 3 silently strengthens per-site locality to the existing all-sites interface.**  
   > “`transferRow_of_readLocality` … already runs the composition — re-point it at the per-site face”

   The cited theorem consumes the rejected all-sites `BridgeReadLocality` shape. “Re-point” suppresses the missing finite-site assembly and the proof that all sites relevant to a row share the required fiber agreement.

8. **BLOCKER — Row 4 never derives CYL from the listed faces.**  
   > “CYL(V) ⇒ (SCALE_T) …”

   The row lists `[P]-thr+[R]`, but its sketch begins by assuming CYL. It therefore proves only `CYL ⇒ count_tie`, not `[P]+[R] ⇒ CYL ⇒ count_tie`.

9. **BLOCKER — Row 5 uses K-READ where run faithfulness is required.**  
   > “`canonical_stable` supply + `VPSound` satisfiability | NsFree+[P]”

   Read locality cannot by itself establish stability of the run roster, existence of halts, sound leaf data, or satisfiability of `VPSound`. This is strictly weaker than the target.

10. **BLOCKER — Row 6 imports certification acceptance into K-RUN.**  
    > “the built predicate accepts the realized run [R]”

    K-RUN states equality of realized and semantic run sets; it says nothing about the separate certification predicate accepting those runs. The sketch silently adds the very OL1-ii agreement seam it claims to derive.

11. **BLOCKER — Row 7 overreads both K-READ-δ and K-DICT.**  
    > “BNS 3.13 gives `N(f) ≤ v_p(disc f)+1` … `[D]` transports to the corpus run”

    BNS gives congruence stability of OM factorizations, not a bound on the stopping time or every read of the corpus run. K-DICT, as stated, matches invariants and refinement nodes; it does not transport execution, reads, termination time, or a whole OM tree.

12. **BLOCKER — Row 8 assumes termination and a uniform complete tree not supplied by `[R]+[P]`.**  
    > “every lift realizes the same complete halted tree”

    Per-site locality plus pointwise run correspondence does not alone establish that the semantic tree terminates, that only finitely many sites must be synchronized, or that the same complete tree is obtained throughout the congruence class.

13. **BLOCKER — Row 11 omits its own LOC dependency.**  
    > “`BK.vp_sound` … | `[R]+[H]+[D] + NsFree`”

    The sketch decomposes VPS using LOC, while row 8 derives LOC only from `[R]+[P]`. Row 11 therefore uses a face strictly weaker than its declared dependency chain by omitting `[P]`.

14. **BLOCKER — Row 12 assumes the missing `inStratum → realized` bridge.**  
    > “verbatim the no-phantom clause at the XFamily surface”

    K-RUN constrains realized runs. The blueprint itself says `inStratum` contains additional branch-history/prefix data not derivable from `XFamily`. Unless membership already implies realization, no-phantom says nothing about arbitrary `inStratum` members. This is the same overreach V1 reportedly rejected.

15. **BLOCKER — Row 13 derives a metric proximity theorem from mere branch membership.**  
    > “cell ⇒ disk at radius `w − C_φ` … the proximity reading of no-phantom”

    No-phantom yields semantic-prefix membership, not the quantitative valuation inequality defining the disk. K-DICT’s invariant matching does not state the required proximity bound either.

16. **BLOCKER — Row 14 reverses soundness into bounded completeness.**  
    > “singleton cluster ⇒ Hensel–Newton certificate fires within slack `κ₀ = 1`”

    K-HALT says what a τ-hen verdict means once such a halt exists. It does not say a singleton cluster causes the certificate to fire, much less by a specified threshold. The face is strictly weaker than X3′.

17. **BLOCKER — Row 15 overstates no-phantom.**  
    > “a continuing node presupposes a repeated residual factor”

    A continuing node being a genuine semantic prefix does not imply repeated residual factorization or wildness unless that semantic theorem is separately present. K-RUN contains no such condition.

18. **ADVISORY — Row 16 does not discharge the counting theorem; it embeds it in K-DICT.**  
    > “the one-to-one counting theorem … the `[D]` carrier extended by the population clause”

    The “population clause” is already the claimed one-to-one theorem. The arrow is projection from a repackaged obligation, not an independent consequence. This is acceptable bookkeeping only if it is not counted as mathematical collapse.

19. **BLOCKER — Row 18 drops K-READ and the remaining MarkGraft duties.**  
    > “`MarkGraft` ⇒ `RealizationComplete` … | `[R]`”

    The sketch immediately says MarkGraft requires `(I0)–(I3)`, while row 17 assigns I2 to `[P]`; I3 also requires a reading-coherence premise, even if later expected to be definitional. `[R]` alone is weaker than the premises acknowledged by the blueprint.

20. **BLOCKER — Row 20 and the U3/U7 story are genuinely circular, not benignly sequenced.**  
    > “`RunRealizerExists` … | `[R]`”  
    > “the bridge-instance discharge waits on the R7 designer data, which itself unblocks via `RunRealizerExists` (= a K-RUN corollary)”  
    > “This circularity is benign — `RunRealizerExists` is provable at the toy instances first”

    A toy-instance existence theorem does not provide `RunRealizerExists` at the bridge instance. If full bridge K-RUN requires the R7 designer data and that designer data requires full bridge `RunRealizerExists`, changing instances does not break the cycle.

21. **ADVISORY — Rows 1, 9, 10, 17, and 19 are plausible projections conditional on precise face definitions.**  
    They are not independent mathematical derivations: L1, ASSEMBLY, the dictionary, and the I-duties are substantially included in the corresponding faces. Row 19 is then ordinary downstream use of `RealizationComplete`.

### Gate ordering

22. **BLOCKER — The cheapest falsification gate is not first.**  
    IFK-U0 lands unrelated MarkGraft material, and U1 only certifies that a known, deliberately excluded all-sites statement is false. Neither probes the proposed kernel. The first unit with a direct real-instance negation criterion is **IFK-U6**, specifically M18 Tests A–C: the blueprint itself says any `T < T̂` length-2 stratum negates K-RUN. That should be the first attempted falsifier. U3’s toy length-1 success is too weak to test the depth-≥2 claim on which the collapse count depends.

### BNS 3.13 draft

23. **BLOCKER — The draft adds conclusions not stated by the published theorem.**  
    Published Theorem 3.13 says that for monic separable `F,G`, congruence modulo `𝔪^(δ(F)+1)` implies `F ≈ G`, and that any OM factorization `F ≈ P₁⋯P_g` is also an OM factorization of `G`. It does not state that all OM representations remain literally valid, that algorithmic OM trees correspond, or that an external classifier statistic `σ` is equal. [Published theorem, pp. 154–155](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/79A4A904C75E875A78F0671E0AF92D9A/S1461157013000089a.pdf/complexity_of_om_factorizations_of_polynomials_over_local_fields.pdf)

24. **BLOCKER — “the OM trees correspond” is a substantial strengthening.**  
    Equality of admissible OM factorizations does not determine equality or correspondence of refinement traces: algorithms can reach the same factorization through different representative choices and refinement histories. This conclusion would import part of K-DICT/K-RUN into the axiom despite §3.2 explicitly forbidding that.

25. **BLOCKER — `σ(f)=σ(g)` is unsupported without a separate invariance theorem.**  
    The publication has no `σ` from this project. Its equality follows only if `σ` has independently been proved invariant under the paper’s Okutsu-equivalence/OM-factorization relation.

26. **ADVISORY — The core congruence clause is otherwise no stronger than the publication.**  
    Restricting the local field to `ℚ_p` and explicitly requiring a common degree `n` narrows the published scope. Coefficient-wise congruence is the expected interpretation of polynomial congruence modulo the maximal-ideal power. The excess strength lies in the representation/tree/`σ` add-ons, not in the `δ+1` hypothesis.

VERDICT: REJECT
